This page documents how the user comments were prepared for coding, how the intercoder reliability (ICR) was tested, and how the final manually coded sample was prepared. For the coding scheme, see [Codebook](appendix_codebook.qmd).

# Manual Coding

## Helper Function

Comments on the website could reply to other comments. To understand a reply, coders need to see the comment it responds to. The function below follows the chain of replies back to the first comment and pastes all comments of the chain together (separated by `>>>`).

```{r}
#| label: reply-chain-function
library(tidyverse)

## def reply chain function
get_reply_chain <- function(df, topic_name, post_num) {
  chain <- c()
  current <- post_num
  visited <- c()
  
  while (!is.na(current) && !current %in% visited) {
    visited <- c(visited, current)
    row <- df |> filter(topic == topic_name, post_number == current)
    if (nrow(row) == 0) break
    chain <- c(chain, row$raw[1])
    current <- row$reply_to_post_number[1]
  }
  
  paste(rev(chain), collapse = " >>> ")
}
```

## Load and Prepare the Comments

The comments were stored separately for each of the three websites (vm1–vm3, one per experimental condition). For each website, we load the comments, remove the threads about the netiquette and the study itself, add the reply chain, and keep only comments written after August 1, 2017.

Website 1:

```{r}
#| label: load-comments-vm1
## data pp 
comments1 <- read_csv("data/comments/data_posts_VM1.csv") |> 
  filter(!str_detect(topic, 
    regex("netiquette | studie", ignore_case = TRUE)))

comments1 <- comments1 |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(reply_chain = if_else(
    !is.na(reply_to_post_number),
    get_reply_chain(comments1, topic, reply_to_post_number),
    NA_character_
  )) |>
  ungroup() |> 
  filter(created_at > as.Date("2017-08-01")) 
```

Website 2:

```{r}
#| label: load-comments-vm2
comments2 <- read_csv("data/comments/data_posts_VM2.csv") |> 
  mutate(created_at = as_datetime(created_at)) |> 
  filter(!str_detect(topic, 
    regex("netiquette | studie", ignore_case = TRUE)))

comments2 <- comments2 |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(reply_chain = if_else(
    !is.na(reply_to_post_number),
    get_reply_chain(comments2, topic, reply_to_post_number),
    NA_character_
  )) |>
  ungroup() |> 
  filter(created_at > as.Date("2017-08-01")) 
```

Website 3:

```{r}
#| label: load-comments-vm3
comments3 <- read_csv("data/comments/data_posts_VM3.csv") |> 
  mutate(created_at = as_datetime(created_at)) |> 
  filter(!str_detect(topic, 
    regex("netiquette | studie", ignore_case = TRUE)))

comments3 <- comments3 |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(reply_chain = if_else(
    !is.na(reply_to_post_number),
    get_reply_chain(comments3, topic, reply_to_post_number),
    NA_character_
  )) |>
  ungroup() |> 
  filter(created_at > as.Date("2017-08-01")) 
```

## Prepare the Coding File

We combine the comments of all three websites and add empty columns for the coder and the six coded variables (personal experience, emotional expression, political opinion, breadth, valence, and controversiality).

```{r}
#| label: prepare-coding-file
## joining all comments
comments <- comments1 |> mutate(vm = "vm1") |> 
  bind_rows(comments2 |> mutate(vm = "vm2")) |>
  bind_rows(comments3 |> mutate(vm = "vm3"))

## prepare coding file 
comments <- comments |>
  mutate(
    coder = NA,
    pers_exp = NA, 
    emot_exp = NA,
    pol_opin = NA,
    breadth = NA,
    valence = NA,
    contr = NA) |> 
  relocate(c(pers_exp:contr), .after = raw) |> 
  relocate(coder, .before = post_number)
```

## Draw the Sample for the Reliability Test

We draw a stratified random sample of 150 comments: 50 per website, hence 50 per experimental condition. Both coders coded this sample independently. All comments and the sample are saved as CSV files.

```{r}
#| label: draw-icr-sample
# weighted sample
set.seed(666)
comments_reli <- comments |> 
  group_by(vm) |> 
  slice_sample(n = 50) |> # 50 per group (vm)
  ungroup() |> 
  select(-c(vm)) |> 
  mutate(unique_id = row_number()) |> 
  relocate(unique_id, .after = coder)


write_csv(comments, "data/comments/comments.csv", na = "")
write_csv(comments_reli, "data/comments/comments_reli.csv", na = "") # write csv for icr test
```

# Intercoder Reliability

## Load the Coded Samples

We load the codings of both coders (J and Y) and combine them into one dataset.

```{r}
#| label: load-codings
coding_j <- readxl::read_excel("data/comments/comments_relij_coded.xlsx")
coding_y <- readxl::read_excel("data/comments/comments_reliy_coded.xlsx")


# set to 5, 20, 50, or 150 for icr tests
# coding_j <- coding_j |> head(150) 
# coding_y <- coding_y |> head(150)


coding_comb <- coding_j |> 
  rbind(coding_y)
```

## Compute Reliability

We compute Krippendorff's alpha, Cohen's kappa, and further agreement measures for each variable. The results are saved for the ICR table in the manuscript.

```{r}
#| label: compute-icr
icr <- coding_comb |> 
  tidycomm::test_icr(unit_var = unique_id, 
                     coder_var = coder, 
                     c(pers_exp:contr), 
                     kripp_alpha = TRUE,
                     cohens_kappa = TRUE,
                     lotus = TRUE, 
                     s_lotus = TRUE, 
                     na.omit = TRUE)

icr
writexl::write_xlsx(icr, "data/comments/icr4.xlsx") # write excel for icr table
```

## Disagreements

To discuss and resolve disagreements, we list all comments where the two coders did not agree on at least one variable.

```{r}
#| label: disagreements
coding_j_red <- coding_j |> 
  select(2, raw, 7:12) |> 
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_j"), .cols = -c(unique_id, raw))

coding_y_red <- coding_y |> 
  select(2, raw,7:12) |> 
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_y"), .cols = -c(unique_id, raw))

disagreement <- coding_j_red |> 
  left_join(coding_y_red, by = c("unique_id", "raw")) |> 
  filter(
    pers_exp_j != pers_exp_y |
    emot_exp_j != emot_exp_y |
    pol_opin_j != pol_opin_y |
    breadth_j != breadth_y |
    valence_j != valence_y |
    contr_j != contr_y 
  
  )


writexl::write_xlsx(disagreement, "data/comments/icr4_disagreement.xlsx")
rm(list = ls())
```

# Final Manual Coding

We load the final manual coding. Missing codes are set to zero (i.e., the feature is absent).

```{r}
#| label: load-final-coding
comments_eval <- readxl::read_excel("data/comments/comments_manual_coding.xlsx")

# remove NAs
comments_eval <- comments_eval |> 
  mutate(across(pers_exp:contr, ~if_else(is.na(.x), 0, .x)))
```

We check whether all comments are coded, by tabulating each variable. The final manual coding is then saved. It is used to evaluate the automatic classifiers (see [Model Comparison](appendix_model_comparison.qmd)).

```{r}
#| label: check-final-coding
# check if everything is coded
vars <- c("pers_exp", "emot_exp", "pol_opin", "breadth", "valence", "contr")

for (v in vars) {
  cat("---", v, "---\n")
  print(table(comments_eval[[v]], useNA = "ifany"))
}

writexl::write_xlsx(comments_eval, "data/comments/comments_eval.xlsx") # use for classifier performance eval
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("comments_eval"))) # clean env
```
